metadata.title: GARCIA_Marleen_2014_2015_WarningAlarm.wav
metadata.description:
HOW I DID IT? --------------------------
Using 3 tracks mixed together: 
First track (3 seconds)
Generate a sound (sinus) : frequency 440 hz - Amplitude 0,8 – duration 3 seconds 
apply effects : Wha-wha = frequency 2,2 – Phase of departure 320 - Depth 23% - Echo 5,3 – Gap of frequency 22%. 
Second track generate a sound (sinus) : frequency 440 hz - Amplitude 0,8 – duration 3 seconds
Export this two tracks together and open it in a new file. 
Then generate the third track
Generate a whistle sound (sinus) starting at 440hz finishing at 1320hz (logarythmic interpolation /3 seconds)
duplicate the sound on the same track but paste it in inverse sense. 
On the first audio track, cross the sound to the left, then to the right for the second audio track. 

HOW CAN I DESCRIBE IT? (French)----------------------
// Typologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) :
X (Continu complexe) + V ( continu Varié)
// Morphologie (Cf. Pierre Schaeffer) :

1- Masse:
- Son "cannelé"

2- Timbre harmonique:
acide 

3- Grain:
lisse

4- Allure:
Le son comporte un vibrato

5- Dynamique :
Attaque et relâchement graduels

6- Profil mélodique:
Variations serpentines d’un côté et scalaire de l’autre

7- Profil de masse
Site :
3 strates de son, deux montant et descendant ensembles et la troisième montant et descendant séparément. 
Calibre :
RAS

metadata.title: DE_LIMA_LUCIO_Romain_2015_2016_revolving_light.wav
metadata.description:
To realize that sound I usead a sinuosidal whistle of 150 Hz generated by Audacity.
Then I duplicated it and reversed the second part. Then, I duplicated the result a few times to get a first track.
Then I duplicated this track 3 times and desynchronysed every track by 3,33 seconds from the previous one, just to give the impression that there were several police cars.

Type de son : Continu Varié (V)
Je trouve ce son éclatant et strident, car il fait bien sur penser au gyrophare de la police, qui est un objet lumineux, et qui n'est pas conçu pour être agréable mais plutot pour être audible.
Le son est parfaitement lisse et ne comporte pas de vibrato. L'attaque du son est abrupte. Les variations sont graduelles, glissantes, il n'y a jamais de véritables ruptures.Le son n'est pas filtré et n'a pas subi d'équalisation.

metadata.title: Kitten 1
metadata.description:
I just pitch up my voice where it's at a comfortable level and not at the highest peak in pitch.

I slowly ease into the vocal sound to avoid any vocal damage.

While I'm easing in there's a very quiet high pitch whistle coming from the back of my throat, too quiet for the microphone.

Sometimes while recording I do get a squeak and a crackle sound that gets picked up, but none of that here.

metadata.title: Scratch Whistling 3 - 2 bar - 90 BPM (swing)
metadata.description:
Acid-sized sample of a scratch made by me. Ready for drag'n'drop music production software.

I recommend you that, if you are going to use it in a track with a different BPM, you change the speed of this sample (like modifying the pitch in a turntable), not just the duration keeping the tone.

Turntable: Vestax PDX-2000MKII Pro
Mixer: Stanton SA.3
Digital system: Rane SL1 (Serato Scratch Live)
Sound card on the PC: M-Audio Audiophile 2496 (sound recorded via analog RCA input)
Recording software: Audacity
Edition software: MAGIX Music Maker 5 / Adobe Audition CS6 (maybe not used)

Scratch sound from a free-royalty scratch sound pack (with lots of classic hip-hop sounds).
